policyPage.title: Expense policy
policyPage.subtitle: What your company reimburses, per category and per client. A category with no cap isn’t “compliant” — it’s unchecked.
policyPage.accountsTruncated: Only the first 200 clients are listed — narrow it down from the client record if yours isn’t here.
policyPage.label: Policy name
policyPage.basisActual: Actual — the receipt is reimbursed, the cap is a warning
policyPage.basisScale: Flat rate — the allowance is reimbursed, whatever the receipt says
policyPage.effectiveFromHint: This revision applies to expenses incurred from this date. Earlier claims keep the policy that was in force.
policyPage.capsHint: An empty field means “no cap” — lines in that category won’t be compared to anything, and the screen will say so. It is not a cap of zero.
policyPage.mileageHint: No scale is supplied: enter the one your company applies. While it’s empty, a mileage allowance stays unchecked — never compliant.
policyPage.historyHint: They stay: a March claim keeps being judged under the March policy.
policyPage.errorDescription: This isn’t “no policy”: the read failed. Try again rather than writing over it.

laura.purpose: Submitted expense reports, how they compare with the scale, and what is left to validate.

guide.title: How to work here
guide.heading: Check a report before reimbursing it
guide.intro: Each line is compared with the workspace scale, or with the scale negotiated with the client. A line without a cap is “not checked”, never compliant.
guide.step1: Open the report: the check has already flagged the gaps.
guide.step2: Read the receipts, then validate or reject — a rejection carries a reason.
guide.step3: Validated expenses enter the mission’s cost.
guide.keep: Validating triggers no reimbursement: the transfer happens in your payroll or your bank.
